1.title: Uruguay's leader talks about Brazil and Mercosur
1.text: Yamandu Orsi is the president of Uruguay. He spoke in Madrid. He said Uruguay's ties with Argentina are excellent. He said Lula's win in Brazil is fundamental. Mercosur is a trade group of South American countries. Its leaders will meet in Montevideo on December 4. But Argentina and Brazil have bad relations now.

2.title: Orsi praises Argentina ties and Lula's re-election before Mercosur summit
2.text:
Uruguayan President Yamandu Orsi spoke in Madrid less than three weeks before the Mercosur summit in Montevideo on December 4. He called his government's relationship with Argentina's Javier Milei "excellent". He said Lula's re-election in Brazil on October 25 is "fundamental".

Orsi said both countries want to make Mercosur, the trade bloc of South America, more flexible. He also gave examples of progress with Argentina, such as work on the access channel to the port of Montevideo.

But tension inside the bloc is strong. Relations between Argentina and Brazil are at their lowest point after Milei's repeated attacks on Lula. Paraguay is also in an institutional crisis. The summit will talk about trade deals with Canada, the United Arab Emirates, Vietnam and Japan. The deal with the European Union has applied provisionally since May 1.

3.title: Orsi praises Milei ties and Lula's re-election ahead of Mercosur summit
3.text:
Uruguayan President Yamandu Orsi described his government's relationship with Javier Milei's administration in Argentina as "excellent" and called Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's October 25 re-election in Brazil "fundamental", in a Mercosur assessment given in Madrid less than three weeks before the bloc's summit in Montevideo on December 4. The remarks were reported by Europa Press.

Orsi, of the left-wing Broad Front, said fluid contact has allowed progress despite "different philosophies", citing dredging of the port access channel and the resolution of tensions over a green hydrogen plant project in Paysandu. He said both governments agree Mercosur should become more flexible and modern. Of Lula's win, he said it is good news because of the positions both candidates took on integration.

The remarks come amid strong tensions in the bloc. Relations between Argentina and Brazil are at their lowest point after Milei's repeated attacks on Lula. Paraguay is also in an institutional crisis after the removal and arrest of President Santiago Pena over the collapse of Ueno Bank. The summit, which closes Uruguay's rotating presidency, is expected to address making the bloc more flexible and trade talks with Canada, the United Arab Emirates, Vietnam and Japan. The European Union agreement has applied provisionally since May 1.
